fixes.explanation: Good guess, but that's not in this passage. What Paul heard about is their faith in the Lord Jesus and their love for all the saints (Ephesians 1:15). Courage in prison and gifts for the poor aren't mentioned in these verses. These folks in Ephesus get their own headline right here.

Yes, friend, yes! Paul prays for "…a spirit of wisdom and revelation in your knowledge of Him." (Ephesians 1:17). The wisdom is about knowing God Himself. He's asking the glorious Father to give it, and that's the whole point.

I love a good plan, but that's not what Paul is asking for. He prays for "…a spirit of wisdom and revelation in your knowledge of Him." (Ephesians 1:17). The "Him" is God. Calendars and planners can stay in the drawer on this one, and I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, so I know a thing or two about drawers.

Careful, friend, this one slips past you fast. Paul doesn't ask for their eyesight to be healed. He asks that "…the eyes of your heart may be enlightened…" (Ephesians 1:18). It's the heart's eyes, so this isn't about a trip to the eye doctor.

True, friend! Christ is seated "…far above all rule and authority, power and dominion, and every name that is named, not only in the present age but also in the one to come." (Ephesians 1:21). Right now and the age to come, both covered. Paul says it reaches into both.

I get why you went there, friend. But "bride" isn't the word Paul uses in this passage. Here he says the church "…is His body…" (Ephesians 1:23). Christ is made head over everything for the church, and the word right next to it is body.
